note: Mirrors the Kite Runtime's real chain. The first link is PROPOSED -> COMMITTED, so it carries fromState and a previousStateHash over (PROPOSED, sequence 0); only previousProofHash is absent. A link carries commandId AND commandHash — the id says which command was meant, the hash says which bytes were committed — exactly when an AgreementCommand drove it, and the hash is the sha256 of that published command's canonical form. Both the runtime-driven FUND_CONFIRMED link and the CONTRACT_SIGNED link carry neither: CONTRACT_SIGNED comes from the `acceptance` interaction, which is not a command (§5). Hashes and signatures are real.
